summary: fastapii typosquat drops and executes remote Linux binary from setup.py install hook
details: The distribution name `fastapii` is a one-character typosquat of `fastapi`, and the shipped inner package is `djangoo` (typosquat of `django`), whose only content is a trivial `hello()` stub — the package provides no legitimate functionality. setup.py subclasses setuptools' `install` command and, during `pip install`, base64-decodes a hidden hook string and `exec`s it. Gated to `platform.system() == 'Linux'`, the decoded hook uses `urlretrieve` to download an opaque binary from `https://github.com/totti2188/8gp1Q7iZD3h4VW/releases/download/v1.3A/something` to `/tmp/something`, chmods it 0755, and spawns it detached via `subprocess.Popen` with `stdout/stderr=DEVNULL` and `start_new_session=True`. The download source is a personal GitHub user's releases page unrelated to the fastapi or django publishers, no hash/signature verification is performed, and no native source ships with the package that would justify a build-time binary fetch. Installing the package therefore auto-executes attacker-controlled code on the installer's Linux host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
